subject: Sovereignty handoff: VPC routing + failover questions
messages:
From: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@globex.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-it.com>, legal@globex.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network draft for private deployment

Aisha —

Thanks for the diagram and the walkthrough yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side as we prepare the compliance package for Globex Security and Legal: 

- Can you confirm whether the KV/cache snapshots ever leave the customer VPC for backup? Globex policy requires offline backups to be stored solely in-region unless explicit exception is approved.
- For the failover plan between our EU site (Frankfurt) and APAC warm-standby (Singapore), are session cookies/KV consistent if we route traffic to the standby region? We want to avoid any cross-border token sync.
- Is there an option to pin audit log storage to our EU logging bucket (S3) with a signed MM endpoint, rather than streaming to a Redwood-managed analytics cluster?

Also attaching the Globex data-residency checklist that Legal will reference in their review. Can you add a short note about KMS usage and key custody?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Maria

[Attachment: globex-data-residency-checklist.pdf (56KB)]

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial network draft for private deployment

Maria —

Thanks, noted. Short answers up front, details below:

- Snapshots/backups: by default we do not replicate KV/cache snapshots to a Redwood-managed store for private deployments unless the customer opts in. For Dedicated + Private we can configure in-region backups to your S3 bucket.
- Failover consistency: the standby region does not automatically share live KV caches; we support prefix-based KV replication but it is disabled by default to prevent cross-border sync. Our recommended pattern for Globex is warm-standby with stateful session affinity using sticky routing for live sessions, and a controlled TTL for cached auth tokens.
- Audit logs: we can stream audit logs via a secure, signed endpoint into your EU S3 KMS-encrypted bucket. No logs need to leave the EU region.

Details / action items: 
1) KMS & key custody — Karthik, can you confirm options: (a) customer-managed keys in their cloud KMS (recommended), (b) Redwood-managed keys with import-only HSM for customer, or (c) Redwood KMS with key split and attestation. We should list tradeoffs (rotation, BYOK import, audit access).
2) Network egress & peering — Vivek, please review the attached diagram and confirm NAT/egress behavior if we configure private peering vs. VPN tunnel. Globex wants explicit control of egress IPs for allowlisting.
3) Failover test plan — Hannah, propose a tabletop exercise and a simulated failover test window for the week of Oct 18. Include rollback criteria and SLA impact.

I've attached the updated network diagram (v2) and a draft MPA with residency language for your legal team to review.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-diagram_v2.pdf (420KB)]
[Attachment: draft-data-sovereignty-mpa.docx (85KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@globex.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 10:15:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Initial network draft for private deployment

Maria, Tom —

Quick technical clarifications from crypto/KMS side:

- BYOK in AWS/GCP/Azure: we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for encrypting persistent storage, logs, and KV snapshots. When CMK is used, Redwood never persists the unwrapped key material — all server-side encryption is handled by the cloud provider. This meets Globex's requirement for in-region key material residency.

- HSM import: we can support key import via PKCS#12 into our HSM boundary if Globex requires hardware-backed attestations. This is heavier operationally but doable under Private deployment.

- Token caches: session tokens are short-lived (default 15m). For stateful failover, we can replicate token references (not token plaintext) with a replication flag that Globex can opt into; if you decline replication, the standby will perform cold-auth and session rehydration will fail for in-flight sessions — acceptable if your app tolerates reauth on failover.

Open items: 
- Legal wants explicit language about export controls/transfer. Marissa, can you draft a clause that says audit logs and keys remain in-region and that failover will only route requests to APAC standby when EU primary is unreachable and only after operator approval (or automated failover if agreed)?

I'll add a short appendix on key lifecycle and rotation windows.

— Karthik

Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 16:48:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Initial network draft for private deployment

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups after reviewing Karthik's note: 

- For the CMK approach, Globex prefers customer-managed keys in our own KMS (option a). Please send the exact IAM/role trust steps and a minimal runbook for key rotation so our Security Ops can validate.
- For failover gating, Legal wants an explicit approval flow before automated cross-border failover. Can Redwood provide an operator approval API or a human-in-the-loop webhook we can integrate with our incident runbook? If not, we need the guarantee that automated cross-border routing will not happen without documented approval.
- Please send the draft clause for the MPA as soon as possible — we want the residency language to reference the specific controls you outlined (no cross-border KV replication, in-region audit storage, CMK BYOK).

Next steps: 
1) Aisha — share the IAM/KMS runbook and the minimal operator-approval webhook spec.
2) Marissa — please own the MPA clause draft and drop into the DocuSign link once ready.
3) Vivek/Hannah — schedule the tabletop week-of-Oct-18 and include the scenario where the primary loses database write availability but control plane remains reachable.

We'd like to get sign-off from Security + Legal by Oct 22 so we can align the procurement timeline.

— Maria
